landing_pages.intro:
Dubai's patients come from many countries and carry different insurance plans. Both shape how they search and which clinic they choose.

  • Insurance first: many patients check whether a clinic accepts their insurance network before comparing doctors or locations.
  • Many languages: searches happen in English and Arabic, and often in Hindi, Malayalam, Urdu or Tagalog too.
  • Licence and credentials: patients look for DHA-licensed doctors, clear specialties and accurate titles on Maps and websites.
  • Area and access: parking, metro access and the drive from home or office influence the final choice.

landing_pages.overview:
How we plan: three steps from first audit to patient walk-ins. We audit what you run today, launch channels by locality, then keep refining against patient visits, not clicks or leads. First you tell us about your clinic — your centres, treatments, targets and the problems you are facing. Then we map the gaps, reviewing your ads, Maps listings, calls and CRM to find where patients drop off. Finally you get a proven plan, with reviews built in.

No office visit needed — we come to your clinic or hospital. Onboarding is compliance-first: we review your DHA licence details, existing ads and Maps profiles with your medical director, then return on an agreed schedule to review patient visits and front-desk handling. Every post and ad goes to your medical director for sign-off before publishing, unanswered calls trigger an automatic WhatsApp reply saved in one patient record, and we use your existing CRM if it tracks source and outcome or switch you to MedLift. We cover Deira, Bur Dubai, Downtown Dubai, Business Bay, Jumeirah, Al Barsha, Dubai Marina, JLT, Mirdif and Al Qusais. To arrange an onboarding visit, call our team on +91 7428094567.

faqs.q: How do you choose the best digital marketing company in Dubai for a clinic?
faqs.a: Do thorough research. Look at client testimonials, a healthcare portfolio and a track record you can verify. Then test its DHA knowledge: the company should know the banned words, title rules and medical director approval process. Ask whether it reports patient visits or stops at leads.

faqs.q: What DHA rules apply to clinic ads on social media?
faqs.a: DHA standards cover posts and ads on platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and WhatsApp. They ban words like "the best" and "100 per cent", require titles to match the DHA licence, and need medical director approval for every post naming a facility.

faqs.q: Can Dubai clinics use patient testimonials and before-and-after photos?
faqs.a: Yes, with conditions. DHA rules require written patient consent, plus separate parental consent for under-18s. Before-and-after photos must show the same person, use the same lens, have no editing and carry a disclaimer that results vary. India's rules are stricter and ban both.

faqs.q: Do these rules apply to clinics in Dubai Healthcare City?
faqs.a: Not in the same way. Facilities in Dubai Healthcare City and DIFC fall under their own regulators rather than the DHA. Their advertising rules differ, so campaigns for these clinics are checked against the framework that applies to their licence.

faqs.q: Should Dubai clinic ads be in Arabic, English or other languages?
faqs.a: Match the languages your patients actually use. English and Arabic cover the base, while Hindi, Malayalam, Urdu or Tagalog ads may suit clinics serving those communities. Run versions side by side and compare patient visits by language, with DHA wording rules applied in each.
